description: Get a daily calendar summary in Slack: the Google Calendar app on paid Slack plans, an automation, or an AI agent that sends tomorrow’s meetings.
h1: How to get a daily calendar summary in Slack
answer: On a paid Slack plan, the Google Calendar for Slack app can send you a daily schedule: open the app’s Home tab, then Settings, and pick the time.
On a free plan, or if you want tomorrow’s meetings the evening before with what to prepare, use an automation or an AI agent that reads your calendar at a set time and sends you a direct message.

body.p: The built-in app is the least work. It sends today’s schedule; if you plan the night before, or want a line on each meeting, build your own.

Whichever you pick, the message is only useful if it arrives when you plan. If you prepare the night before, send it around 18:00; if you plan in the morning, send it before your first meeting, not at midnight when nobody reads it.

method.h2: How to set it up, step by step

steps.title: Pick the calendar and the window
steps.body: Your primary calendar, or a shared team one. Today from 00:00 to 23:59, or tomorrow, in your timezone.

steps.title: Pick the time
steps.body: 18:00 for tomorrow lets you prepare tonight; 8:00 for today is a morning check.

steps.title: Send it to yourself, not a channel
steps.body: A direct message keeps private event titles private. Post team schedules to a channel only from a team calendar.

steps.title: Decide what each line shows
steps.body: Time, title, who, and where (room or video link). Skip descriptions; they are long and often private.

steps.title: Handle the edge cases
steps.body: All-day events, declined invites, recurring events moved this once, and travel across timezones. Test a day with each.

body: In 50agents this is an AI agent: Captain builds it from one sentence with Google Calendar and Slack. Each evening it reads tomorrow’s meetings and sends you one message: the meetings in order, any clash, and anything worth preparing. If a step would reach other people, it asks you first.

wrong.title: No schedule on free Slack
wrong.body: The Google Calendar app’s daily schedule needs a paid plan. Use an automation or an AI agent instead.

wrong.title: Times off by an hour
wrong.body: The tool used UTC or the wrong timezone. Set the window and the send time in your timezone.

wrong.title: Private events in a channel
wrong.body: "Doctor" or "Interview: Jane Doe" posted for the team. Send personal schedules as direct messages.

wrong.title: Declined meetings still listed
wrong.body: Filter out events you declined, and say which are tentative.

wrong.title: Status sync fights you
wrong.body: Slack’s calendar status follows your primary calendar only and will not override a status you set yourself, according to Slack’s help. Expect gaps there.

faqs.q: Can Slack show my daily schedule?
faqs.a: Yes, on paid plans, through the Google Calendar for Slack app’s daily schedule notification. Turn it on in the app’s Home tab, under Settings.

faqs.q: Can I get tomorrow’s meetings the night before?
faqs.a: Not from the built-in app, which sends today’s schedule. An automation or AI agent on an evening schedule can.

faqs.q: Does it work with Outlook calendars?
faqs.a: Slack has an Outlook Calendar app too, and automation tools connect to Outlook. The steps above are the same.

faqs.q: What should a daily schedule message include?
faqs.a: Each meeting’s time, title, who is in it and where, in order, with clashes and long gaps called out. Leave out descriptions: they are long and often private.

faqs.q: Should the summary go to a channel or a direct message?
faqs.a: A direct message for your own calendar, so private titles stay private. A channel only for a shared team calendar, with titles everyone may see.
